title: Hybrid bank: on-premises core and two clouds

organisation.name: Northmere Bank
organisation.size: 2,600 staff; 40-person IT security team with a managed SOC partner
organisation.summary: Northmere Bank runs its core banking system and payments messaging gateway in its own data centre, with signing keys in an HSM and admin access through a PAM vault. Active Directory is synchronised to a cloud identity provider that signs staff in to the digital banking cloud, where the mobile and web banking pods run on Kubernetes and deploy from CI. A nightly ETL job copies core data to a customer data warehouse in a second cloud for analysts. A managed service provider runs desktop support through a remote-management tool, and the SOC watches a SIEM with automated playbooks.

controls.label: EDR
controls.covers: Malware and hands-on-keyboard activity on laptops
controls.limits: The RMM agent is allow-listed, so scripts it runs are neither blocked nor alerted

controls.label: session recording
controls.covers: Admin sessions to the core banking system and AD that go through PAM
controls.limits: Only sessions through PAM; the RMM agent reaches laptops directly and AD admins can sign in without it

controls.label: MFA
controls.limits: Not enforced for the sync account, and passwords synced from AD are accepted as the first factor

controls.label: dual control
controls.covers: Signing keys never leave the HSM; key changes need two operators
controls.limits: Signs whatever the payments gateway submits; it does not check the payment

controls.label: WAF
controls.covers: Common web attacks on digital banking

controls.label: segmentation
controls.covers: The core accepts connections only from PAM, the payments gateway and the banking link
controls.limits: The nightly ETL connection from the analytics cloud is also allowed

controls.label: SOAR playbooks
controls.covers: Automatic laptop isolation on high EDR alerts
controls.limits: No playbooks or log feeds for the cloud IdP, CI or the warehouse

controls.label: column masking
controls.covers: Masks account and ID numbers in reporting views
controls.limits: Not applied to the raw staging tables the ETL loads

controls.label: admin tiering
controls.covers: Keeping domain admin credentials off ordinary laptops

controls.label: image signing
controls.covers: Only signed images run in the banking cluster

identity_access.summary: Domain compromise reaches the sync server, which can reset any cloud identity
An identity written through the sync account reaches analyst access to the warehouse

cloud_security.summary: A cloud admin created through the sync account changes the deploy pipeline
The ETL job's database password links the analytics cloud to the core

network_security.summary: The core segment lets the ETL host in, and the payments gateway is one hop further
The MSP's remote-management agent opens a route from the vendor to laptops and on to the domain

zero_trust.summary: The core trusts anything presenting the cluster's client secret over the private link
Vendor sessions are trusted because they come through the MSP tool, not because of who is on them

security_operations.summary: An attacker moves from a laptop to the domain and the sync server; which signals reach the SIEM?
Cloud IdP role grants and warehouse queries never reach the SIEM

incident_response.summary: Ransomware staged through the MSP agent spreads from laptops toward the domain
Fraudulent payment messages are signed after an admin session reaches the core

threat_intelligence.summary: A threat report describes a group abusing MSP remote-management tools against banks
Intelligence on payment-messaging fraud names the gateway and its operators as targets

grc_risk.summary: The MSP's access is broader than its contract and is never reviewed
Raw customer data in the warehouse staging tables is not masked

data_security.summary: Unmasked staging tables are reachable with any identity the sync account can create
The ETL's read account can extract every account and transaction from the core

endpoint_security.summary: A script pushed through the allow-listed RMM agent runs on laptops with no EDR block
Domain admins sign in to ordinary laptops, so a laptop's LSASS holds domain credentials

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: A cloud identity created through sync abuse approves and runs a deploy
Without image signing, a tampered image reaches the banking pods and their core credentials

reviewNotes: Advanced: two subtle trusts (AD to cloud through the sync server; the MSP agent bypassing PAM and EDR) and a third (ETL opening the core segment). Present controls that do not apply: EDR allow-lists the RMM agent, PAM recording misses agent sessions, MFA excludes the sync account, masking skips staging tables.
